biography: Gerrard Andrewes (1750–1825) was educated at Westminster and Trinity College, Cambridge. He was ordained deacon in 1776 and priest in 1778.
During his Mickleham incumbency he also became Rector of St James’s Piccadilly in 1802 and Dean of Canterbury in 1809.
didYouKnow: He was offered the Bishopric of Chester in 1812 and declined it.

biography: Alfred Burmester served as Rector of Mickleham for approximately 54 years. He is buried in a vault beneath the chancel with his wife Jane and two sons who died in infancy.
parishContext: His ministry coincided with substantial nineteenth-century rebuilding and restoration at St Michael’s.
didYouKnow: Woodwork he obtained in Belgium around 1840 was later incorporated into the church pulpit.

parishContext: In 1929, 27 candidates were presented for confirmation.
didYouKnow: A parish account from 1925 describes a water-powered church organ and pressure problems after houses were built in Dell Close.

biography: John Harkin served Mickleham during two separate periods: 1993–1998 and 2018–2020.

Appointment reporting from 1998 identifies him as Priest-in-Charge of Mickleham and Chaplain of Box Hill School when he left for Jersey. Parish material from 2018 describes his return after twenty years.

biography: Malcolm Raby came to Mickleham in June 2013 as a house-for-duty priest after retiring from full-time ministry as Vicar of Over and Longstanton in the Diocese of Ely.
He lived in the parsonage and undertook parish duties without stipend under the house-for-duty arrangement. Parish material announced his retirement in November 2017.
